edges.effect_quant: The performance benefit is usually small but repeatable in glycolytic tasks, especially when exercise lasts long enough for acid buffering to matter.
edges.mechanism: Sodium bicarbonate raises extracellular bicarbonate and pH, which increases the gradient for hydrogen-ion efflux from heavily working muscle. That matters most in repeated or sustained high-intensity efforts where intracellular acidosis contributes to fatigue, not in very short maximal bursts where buffering has little time to help.
edges.summary: The literature does not support a miracle effect, but it does support a real one. Meta-analyses consistently show that sodium bicarbonate can improve anaerobic or muscular-endurance performance by a small-to-moderate amount, with the clearest gains in events lasting roughly half a minute to several minutes.
edges.caveats: Gastrointestinal intolerance is common and can erase any ergogenic benefit in practice. Effects also vary by event duration, training status, and whether the athlete achieves a meaningful bicarbonate rise before exercise.
